title: Update rule-naming documentation for the origin/id split
description:
`docs/reference/configuration.md` and `docs/reference/labels.md` document the fixed default rule set using its old colon-embedded names (e.g. `default:namespace-registry`, `default:namespace-unique:<ns>`). Once rule identity splits origin out of the id (a colon-free `name` plus a separate `origin` field, e.g. `label-format` with origin `default`, `namespace-unique-<ns>` with origin `default`), these references go stale.

Update:
- `docs/reference/configuration.md:108` — the sentence describing the namespace registry driving `default:namespace-registry` and `default:namespace-unique:*` to the colon-free names `namespace-registry` and `namespace-unique-<ns>`.
- `docs/reference/labels.md:168` — "Drives the `default:namespace-unique:<ns>` rule" to "Drives the `namespace-unique-<ns>` rule".
- `docs/reference/labels.md:172-173` — the `default:namespace-registry` / `default:namespace-unique:<ns>` rule-name references to their colon-free equivalents.
- `docs/reference/labels.md:195` — "the `default:namespace-registry` rule names the offending label" to "the `namespace-registry` rule names the offending label".

Also add a short note near these references that a rule's origin (`default`/`bracket`) is a separate field on its `.jit/rules.toml` entry, not part of its name, and that rules are addressable at `@/rule/<self-id>`.

## Success Criteria
- [hard] REQ-01: `docs/reference/configuration.md` and `docs/reference/labels.md` reference only colon-free rule names (`namespace-registry`, `namespace-unique-<ns>`, `label-format`, `type-hierarchy-known`, `orphan-leaf`, `strategic-consistency`, `coverage-preview`); a grep for `default:namespace-registry`, `default:namespace-unique`, `default:label-format`, `default:type-hierarchy-known`, `default:orphan-leaf`, `default:strategic-consistency`, or `bracket:coverage-preview` under `docs/` returns no hits.
- [hard] REQ-02: the updated docs state that a rule's origin is a separate schema field and that rules resolve at `@/rule/<self-id>`.
